clue.text: Is in control of distant armies abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered far and wide, so the letters of the two words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A general commands far-flung troops serving overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' reworks the thirteen letters of DISTANT ARMIES. 'Armies abroad' reads as troops overseas, hiding the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to manage or run something, which is being in control of it.

clue.text: Import teak, say, brought in by sea

definitions.text: Import teak, say, brought in by sea

parts.words: Import teak, say, brought in by sea
parts.note: reads like timber shipped in by trade, but means timber that the waves themselves carry to the shore

explanation.surface: A merchant ships teak in from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' suggests commerce; the sea here is the carrier, washing timber up on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood floating in the sea and washed ashore is the material the clue's cryptic reading describes.

clue.text: Girl providing passion to one lacking love

parts.note: passion in the sense of anger or rage is ire

indicators.note: lacking means the following word is missing a letter that the clue names

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman brings fiery feeling to a lonely, loveless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking love' takes O out of ONE, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: If a plan goes awry, you might be

definitions.text: If a plan goes awry, you might be

indicators.note: a plan going awry is falling into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: When your scheme falls apart you are likely to panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes awry' rearranges IF A PLAN; the whole clue also tells you how you would feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated and panicky is the state a ruined plan leaves you in, which is the whole clue's sense.

clue.text: Syrup well described by the Dormouse

definitions.text: Syrup well described by the Dormouse

parts.words: Syrup well described by the Dormouse
parts.note: in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters living at the bottom of a well full of this syrup

explanation.surface: A storyteller depicts a spring of sweet syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' seems an adverb (described well) but is a noun: the Dormouse's story at the Mad Hatter's tea party features a well of this.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a thick dark syrup, the substance filling the Dormouse's well in Lewis Carroll's tale.

clue.text: Right to enter guilty plea

definitions.meaning: permission to go into a place, such as entry to a club or show
a confession of wrongdoing in court

explanation.surface: A lawyer argues entitlement to make a plea of guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both permission to go in and an acknowledgment of guilt, two distinct senses.

clue.text: Given voice to provide some conclusive words

indicators.note: the answer supplies some of the letters of the phrase before it, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A speaker is allowed to say a few closing remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide some' points to letters inside giVEN VOIce.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is a short concluding stanza of a poem, a set of closing words.

clue.text: Once again sort out those of a certain age

indicators.note: sort out here means arrange anew, so these letters are put into another order

explanation.surface: A clerk re-sorts the records of elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' tempts as a phrase; 'sort' is fodder with ONCE AGAIN and 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Octogenarians are people in their eighties, a particular age bracket the definition coyly hints at.

clue.text: He finds suitable digs before starting work

definitions.text: He finds suitable digs before starting work

parts.words: He finds suitable digs before starting work
parts.note: reads like someone finding lodgings before a new job, but the digs are excavation sites

explanation.surface: A new employee hunts for lodgings before taking up the job.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English 'digs' are rented lodgings; here they are excavations.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaeologist chooses excavation sites and then works on them, which fits the second reading.

clue.text: Part of the tide of lawlessness?

definitions.text: Part of the tide of lawlessness?

parts.words: Part of the tide of lawlessness?
parts.note: a tide is made of breakers, so a surge of offending is pictured as one of them

explanation.surface: A commentator describes a rising tide of disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise in offences is called a surge, the watery metaphor the clue extends.

clue.text: One who proposes to go on board mid-April

parts.note: a go in chess or draughts on the board is a move

indicators.note: mid- takes the central letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A suitor plans to embark on a ship in the middle of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go on board' suggests embarking; it is a turn in a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: In a meeting the person who formally proposes a motion is called its mover.

clue.text: Striking centre spread that's way out

parts.note: workers striking are said to be out

indicators.note: centre takes the middle two letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A magazine's eye-catching middle pages are very unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre spread' looks like a magazine's middle pages; 'centre' picks RE from sprEAd's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre means bizarre or unconventional, which is colloquially way out.

clue.text: Key worker at the hairdressers?

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair, so someone working them is jokingly a craftsman of them; really a maker of keys and locks

explanation.surface: An essential employee at a salon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' sounds like an essential staffer; it is one who works with keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who makes and repairs locks and keys, pictured punningly as shaping locks of hair.

clue.text: An over self-indulgent action to gripe about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Moaning about something can be a vain indulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TO GRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is something done mainly to boost one's own vanity.

clue.text: A quasi-stellar object — like Terry Wogan?

definitions.meaning: a quasar, a distant celestial source of strong radio waves
Terry Wogan was a famous BBC radio presenter, a celebrity of the airwaves

explanation.surface: Asks whether a popular broadcaster is like a quasar.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Wogan was a long-serving, much-loved BBC Radio 2 breakfast host.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a celestial radio source and a celebrity broadcaster, two different senses.

clue.text: Mince pie and preserve for the gourmet

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so these letters are cut and rearranged

parts.note: to preserve meat by salting or smoking is to cure it

explanation.surface: A festive mince pie with jam to delight a food lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pie' looks like the Christmas pastry; 'Mince' is the verb rearranging PIE into EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person devoted to refined food and drink, a connoisseur of fine eating.

clue.text: Turned up in shocking condition?

definitions.meaning: an electrical appliance lacking a connection to ground can give a shock

explanation.surface: Something was found in a dreadful state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' suggests appalling; it means liable to give an electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means discovered, and also lacking a ground connection, so dangerous electrically.

clue.text: Came to a total that made sense

explanation.surface: Figures that totalled correctly and were coherent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both summed to and was logically consistent.

clue.text: Remains within easy reach of Naples

definitions.text: Remains within easy reach of Naples

parts.words: Remains within easy reach of Naples
parts.note: reads as staying close to the Italian city, but means ruins near it

explanation.surface: Someone stays close to the Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb; it is a noun, ancient ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii is the buried Roman town whose ruins lie near Naples below Vesuvius.

clue.text: Polite chap goes to fish

parts.note: a chap is a man, a gent
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A courteous man goes fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means refined and well-mannered, a synonym of polite.

clue.text: There's a tonic in eggs scrambled around mid-morning

indicators.note: around places the scrambled letters on either side of the next piece
scrambled eggs suggests breakfast, but here signals the letters being mixed up
mid- takes the central letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Breakfast includes scrambled eggs with a health tonic mid-morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' makes GISENG, which goes 'around' N; 'scrambled eggs' reads as breakfast, hiding the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a root used as a restorative, regarded as a tonic.

clue.text: Starting place for the three-legged race?

definitions.text: Starting place for the three-legged race?

parts.words: Starting place for the three-legged race?
parts.note: the three-legged emblem is the symbol of a self-governing island, so its people are pictured as a race with three legs

explanation.surface: Asks where a school sports day event begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is a people, not a contest; the island in the Irish Sea has a three-legged symbol, the triskelion.
explanation.definitionFit: This Crown dependency's flag shows three legs, so its people are humorously that race.

clue.text: Fifty, in turn, give tongue

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written
a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Fifty dogs take turns barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give tongue' is hounds barking; 'tongue' alone is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language, and a tongue is a language.

clue.text: Twig a starting price swindle

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price, the odds when a race begins
to rig is to fix fraudulently, a swindle

explanation.surface: Someone cottons on to a fixed betting price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like a verb, to understand; it is a noun, a small shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or spray of a plant, much like a twig.

clue.text: Opera house provided extract of Tosca last year

indicators.note: an extract is a portion taken out, so the answer is letters drawn from inside the words

explanation.surface: An opera house staged a scene from Puccini's opera last year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extract of' points to letters inside toSCA LAst; 'year' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is one of the world's most famous opera houses.

clue.text: Musical composition to catch on the heart

indicators.note: the heart means the following word is placed in the middle of the catching word

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: A piece of music that captures the emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart' puts ON in the middle of NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece of music written for nine performers.

clue.text: Look! He's being taken in by girl, who is fluttering them?

parts.note: to look is to eye something

indicators.note: being taken in places the pronoun inside the word for a girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
the pronoun he, with the apostrophe s serving the surface only

explanation.surface: A flirtatious girl draws a man in by fluttering at him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken in by' signals the container. The definition only works with the whole picture: the girl is fluttering them, so it points to what a flirt flutters.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette flutters the fine hairs fringing her eyelids, so the question points at them.

clue.text: Type of school game obligatory for most high-fliers

parts.note: a boarding school is one where pupils live during term
cards is a game played with a pack

explanation.surface: A school with a compulsory game for its high achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-fliers' seems to mean achievers; it means air passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Air passengers must show the pass that lets them board a plane, so it is required for flyers.
